```{r}
library(httr2)
library(jsonlite)
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)
library(purrr)
library(sf)
library(leaflet)
library(viridis)

url <- "https://power.larc.nasa.gov/api/temporal/daily/point?parameters=T2M,PRECTOTCORR&community=RE&longitude=-77.0369&latitude=38.9072&start=19900101&end=20251231&format=JSON"

# Fetch and parse JSON
resp <- request(url) |> req_perform()
parsed <- resp_body_json(resp)

# Extract parameters list (e.g., T2M, PRECTOTCORR)
param_list <- parsed$properties$parameter

# Convert each parameter list into a tidy tibble and merge by date
climate_df <- map(names(param_list), function(param_name) {
  p_data <- param_list[[param_name]]
  tibble(
    date_str = names(p_data),
    value = unlist(p_data)
  ) |> 
    rename(!!param_name := value)
}) |> 
  reduce(full_join, by = "date_str") |> 
  mutate(date = as.Date(date_str, format = "%Y%m%d")) |> 
  select(-date_str) |> 
  relocate(date)

# Check the dimensions now (should be ~13,000 rows by 3 columns)
dim(climate_df)
head(climate_df)
NASA.data <- climate_df
```

view(climate_df)

```{r}
library(httr2)
library(jsonlite)

# 1. Define your parameters
# Example: Station ID for Central Park, NY (USW00094728)
station_id <- "USW00094728"
start_date <- "2025-01-01"
end_date   <- "2025-01-31"

# 2. Build the request for NCEI's Data Service API v1
base_url <- "https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/access/services/data/v1"

req <- request(base_url) |>
  req_url_query(
    dataset        = "daily-summaries",
    stations       = station_id,
    startDate      = start_date,
    endDate        = end_date,
    dataTypes      = "TMAX,TMIN,PRCP", # Specify exactly what variables you want
    format         = "json",
    units          = "standard",       # Or "metric"
    includeAttributes = "false"
  )

# 3. Perform the request and check the response
resp <- req_perform(req)

# 4. Parse the JSON response directly into an R data frame
weather_data <- resp_body_json(resp, simplifyVector = TRUE)

# View the first few rows of your targeted dataset
head(weather_data)
```

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(httr2)
library(jsonlite)

# 1. Assume Census.data is already loaded from your Gazetteer zip download
# Let's filter for a test vector of major cities or extract top N populous cities
# (Census Gazetteer columns typically include USPS, NAME, INTPTLAT, INTPTLONG)

target_cities <- Census.data |>
  filter(USPS %in% c("DC", "NY", "IL", "CA", "TX")) |> # Example state filter or select top cities
  select(name = USPS, city_name = NAME, lat = INTPTLAT, lon = INTPTLONG) |>
  mutate(
    lat = as.numeric(lat),
    lon = as.numeric(lon)
  ) |>
  head(5) # Limit to 5 for initial testing

# 2. Generalize your NASA POWER fetch function to accept lat/lon dynamically
get_nasa_power_city <- function(city_name, lat, lon, start = "19900101", end = "20251231") {
  url <- sprintf(
    "https://power.larc.nasa.gov/api/temporal/daily/point?parameters=T2M,T2M_MAX,T2M_MIN,PRECTOTCORR,QV2M&community=RE&longitude=%f&latitude=%f&start=%s&end=%s&format=JSON",
    lon, lat, start, end
  )
  
  tryCatch({
    resp <- request(url) |> req_perform()
    parsed <- resp_body_json(resp)
    param_list <- parsed$properties$parameter
    
    # Map parameters into a tibble
    city_df <- map(names(param_list), function(param_name) {
      p_data <- param_list[[param_name]]
      tibble(
        date_str = names(p_data),
        value = unlist(p_data)
      ) |> rename(!!param_name := value)
    }) |>
      reduce(full_join, by = "date_str") |>
      mutate(
        date = as.Date(date_str, format = "%Y%m%d"),
        city = city_name
      ) |>
      select(-date_str) |>
      relocate(city, date)
    
    return(city_df)
  }, error = function(e) {
    message(paste("Error fetching data for", city_name, ":", e$message))
    return(NULL)
  })
}

# 3. Iterate across all target cities using purrr::pmap or map2
all_cities_nasa <- pmap_dfr(
  target_cities, 
  ~ get_nasa_power_city(..2, ..3, ..4)
)

head(all_cities_nasa)
```

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)

# 1. Prepare target city coordinates from Census Gazetteer data
# (Assuming gaz_data is already loaded from your Gazetteer zip download)
city_coords <- gaz_data |>
  filter(USPS %in% c("DC", "NY", "IL", "CA", "TX")) |> # Filter for target states or cities
  select(state = USPS, city_name = NAME, lat = INTPTLAT, lon = INTPTLONG) |>
  mutate(
    lat = as.numeric(lat),
    lon = as.numeric(lon)
  ) |>
  drop_na(lat, lon)

# Convert cities data frame to an sf spatial object (WGS 84 coordinate reference system)
cities_sf <- st_as_sf(city_coords, coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326)

# 2. Download and parse the NOAA GHCN station inventory metadata
stations_url <- "https://www1.ncdc.noaa.gov/pub/data/ghcn/daily/ghcnd-stations.txt"
col_widths <- c(11, 9, 9, 7, 31, 4, 4, 5)
col_names <- c("station_id", "lat", "lon", "elevation", "state", "name", "gsn_flag", "wmo_id")

stations_df <- read_fwf(stations_url, col_positions = fwf_widths(col_widths, col_names)) |>
  filter(str_starts(station_id, "US")) # Keep U.S. stations only

# Convert stations data frame into an sf spatial object
stations_sf <- sf::st_as_sf(stations_df, coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326)

# 3. Find the nearest GHCN station index for each city point
nearest_idx <- st_nearest_feature(cities_sf, stations_sf)

# 4. Merge city metadata with the matched station records and calculate distance
matched_stations <- cities_sf |>
  mutate(
    station_id   = stations_df$station_id[nearest_idx],
    station_name = stations_df$name[nearest_idx],
    station_lat  = stations_df$lat[nearest_idx],
    station_lon  = stations_df$lon[nearest_idx],
    # Calculate exact great-circle distance in kilometers between city and station
    distance_km  = as.numeric(st_distance(cities_sf, stations_sf[nearest_idx, ], by_element = TRUE)) / 1000
  ) |>
  st_drop_geometry() # Convert back to a clean data frame tibble

# Inspect the final matched table
print(matched_stations)
```

stations_url <- "https://www1.ncdc.noaa.gov/pub/data/ghcn/daily/ghcnd-stations.txt"
col_widths <- c(11, 9, 9, 7, 31, 4, 4, 5)

# ==============================================================================
# 3. BATCH FETCH NASA POWER CLIMATE DATA ACROSS ALL 50 CITIES
# ==============================================================================
get_nasa_power_city <- function(city_name, lat, lon, start = "19900101", end = format(Sys.Date(), "%Y%m%d")) {
  url <- sprintf(
    "https://power.larc.nasa.gov/api/temporal/daily/point?parameters=T2M,T2M_MAX,T2M_MIN,PRECTOTCORR,QV2M&community=RE&longitude=%f&latitude=%f&start=%s&end=%s&format=JSON",
    lon, lat, start, end
  )
  
  tryCatch({
    resp <- request(url) |> req_perform()
    parsed <- resp_body_json(resp)
    param_list <- parsed$properties$parameter
    
    map(names(param_list), function(param_name) {
      p_data <- param_list[[param_name]]
      tibble(date_str = names(p_data), value = unlist(p_data)) |> 
        rename(!!param_name := value)
    }) |>
      reduce(full_join, by = "date_str") |>
      mutate(
        date = as.Date(date_str, format = "%Y%m%d"),
        city = city_name
      ) |>
      select(-date_str) |>
      relocate(city, date)
  }, error = function(e) {
    message(paste("Error fetching data for", city_name, ":", e$message))
    return(NULL)
  })
}

# Run batch pull across all 50 cities using pmap_dfr
# (Note: For all 50 cities, this may take 1-2 minutes to query safely)
all_cities_nasa <- pmap_dfr(
  top_50_cities, 
  ~ get_nasa_power_city(..1, ..3, ..4)
)

print("NASA Climate Data Panel Preview:")
print(head(all_cities_nasa))

  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
      width = 3,
      h4("Dashboard Controls"),
      
      # City selection (populated dynamically from successfully pulled cities)
      selectInput(
        inputId = "selected_city",
        label = "Select City:",

      # Climate metric selection

# ==============================================================================
# SERVER LOGIC
# ==============================================================================
server <- function(input, output, session) {
  
  # Reactive filtered dataset based on city and date range
  filtered_data <- reactive({
    req(input$selected_city, input$date_range)
    all_cities_nasa |>
      filter(
        city == input$selected_city,
        date >= input$date_range[1],
        date <= input$date_range[2]
      )
  })
  
  # Reactive station metadata for the selected city
  selected_station <- reactive({
    req(input$selected_city)
    matched_stations |>
      filter(city == input$selected_city)
  })
  
  # Tab 1: Time Series Plot
  output$time_series_plot <- renderPlot({
    df <- filtered_data()
    req(nrow(df) > 0)
    
    metric_label <- case_when(
      input$climate_metric == "T2M" ~ "Mean Temperature (°C)",
      input$climate_metric == "T2M_MAX" ~ "Max Temperature (°C)",
      input$climate_metric == "T2M_MIN" ~ "Min Temperature (°C)",
      input$climate_metric == "PRECTOTCORR" ~ "Precipitation (mm/day)",
      input$climate_metric == "QV2M" ~ "Specific Humidity (g/kg)",
      TRUE ~ input$climate_metric
    )
    
    ggplot(df, aes(x = date, y = .data[[input$climate_metric]])) +
      geom_line(color = "#2c3e50", alpha = 0.7, linewidth = 0.5) +
      geom_smooth(method = "loess", color = "#e74c3c", se = TRUE, span = 0.2) +
      theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
      labs(
        title = paste("Climate Trend for", input$selected_city),
        subtitle = paste("Metric:", metric_label),
        x = "Date",
        y = metric_label
      ) +
      theme(
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
      )
  })
  
  # Tab 1: Summary Statistics
  output$summary_stats <- renderPrint({
    df <- filtered_data()
    req(nrow(df) > 0)
    summary(df[[input$climate_metric]])
  })
  
  # Tab 1: Station Metadata Table
  output$station_meta_table <- renderTable({
    st <- selected_station()
    req(nrow(st) > 0)
    st |>
      mutate(distance_km = round(distance_km, 2)) |>
      rename(
        City = city,
        State = state,
        Lat = lat,
        Lon = lon,
        "NOAA ID" = station_id,
        "Station Name" = station_name,
        "Distance (km)" = distance_km
      )
  })
  
  # Tab 2: Regression Plot
  output$regression_plot <- renderPlot({
    df <- filtered_data()
    req(nrow(df) > 0)
    
    ggplot(df, aes(x = date, y = .data[[input$climate_metric]])) +
      geom_point(alpha = 0.3, color = "#7f8c8d", size = 1) +
      geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "#2980b9", se = TRUE, linewidth = 1) +
      theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
      labs(
        title = paste("Linear Trend Analysis:", input$selected_city),
        subtitle = "Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) Fit over Selected Date Range",
        x = "Date",
        y = input$climate_metric
      ) +
      theme(
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
      )
  })
  
  # Tab 2: Model Summary
  output$model_summary <- renderPrint({
    df <- filtered_data()
    req(nrow(df) > 0)
    
    formula_obj <- reformulate("date", response = input$climate_metric)
    model <- lm(formula_obj, data = df)
    summary(model)
  })
  
  # Map Output (Using OpenStreetMap tiles to prevent API key errors)
  output$climate_map <- renderLeaflet({
    metric <- input$climate_metric
    
    map_data <- all_cities_nasa |>
      inner_join(top_50_cities, by = "city") |>
      group_by(city, state, lat, lon) |>
      summarize(
        temp_change = {
          fit <- lm(.data[[metric]] ~ as.numeric(date))
          coef(fit)[2] * 365.25 * 10 # Net change per decade (°C/decade)
        },
        .groups = "drop"
      ) |>
      drop_na(lat, lon, temp_change)
    
    pal <- colorNumeric(
      palette = "RdBu", 
      domain = map_data$temp_change,
      reverse = TRUE # Blue for cooling, Red for warming
    )
    
    leaflet(map_data) |>
      addProviderTiles(providers$OpenStreetMap.Mapnik) |>
      setView(lng = -98.5795, lat = 39.8283, zoom = 4) |>
      addCircleMarkers(
        lng = ~lon,
        lat = ~lat,
        radius = 8,
        color = ~pal(temp_change),
        stroke = TRUE,
        weight = 1,
        fillOpacity = 0.8,
        popup = ~paste0(
          "<strong>City: </strong>", city, ", ", state, "<br>",
          "<strong>Metric: </strong>", metric, "<br>",
          "<strong>Trend: </strong>", round(temp_change, 3), " °C / decade"
        )
      ) |>
      addLegend(
        position = "bottomright",
        pal = pal,
        values = ~temp_change,
        title = "Temp Change<br>(°C / Decade)",
        opacity = 1
      )
  })
  
  # Tab 3: Raw Data Table
  output$raw_data_table <- renderDT({
    datatable(
      filtered_data(),
      options = list(pageLength = 15, scrollX = TRUE),
      rownames = FALSE
    )
  })
}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
